summary_en.motivation: This paper aims to achieve integrated control of melt pool geometry and microstructure in laser powder bed fusion of AlSi10Mg.
summary_en.method: The study varies LPBF process parameters to influence melt pool characteristics and solidification microstructure.

papers.title: Wrapping effect of secondary phases on the grains: increased corrosion resistance of Mg–Al alloys
papers.abstract: The discrete secondary phases usually cause severe galvanic corrosion, thereby resulting in rapid degradation for Mg–Al alloys in orthopaedics application. In this study, CaO was introduced into Mg–Al–Zn (AZ61) alloy via selective laser melting (SLM) to ameliorate the characterisations of the secondary phases, with an aim to improve its corrosion behaviour. Results revealed that CaO reacted with Mg and Al in Mg–Al alloys during SLM, suppressing the formation of coarse Mg17Al12 phase and promoting the formation of (Mg, Al)2Ca phase. Meanwhile, the rapid solidification during SLM promoted the homogeneous precipitation of the second phase. As a result, inert (Mg, Al)2Ca phase homogeneously wrapped the Mg grains, which effectively protected them from the invasion of corrosion solution. Thus, the degradation rate was remarkably reduced from 0.073 to 0.031 mg cm–2 h–1. Furthermore, AZ61-9CaO exhibited good cytocompatibility. This work suggested that AZ61-9CaO was promising candidates for orthopaedics implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 改善镁合金植入物的耐腐蚀性以降低降解速率

summary_en.motivation: To enhance the corrosion resistance of Mg-Al alloys for biodegradable orthopaedic implants by modifying secondary phase characteristics.
summary_en.method: CaO was introduced into AZ61 alloy via selective laser melting, promoting the formation of (Mg, Al)2Ca phase that homogeneously wraps Mg grains.
summary_en.result: The degradation rate was reduced from 0.073 to 0.031 mg cm–2 h–1, and the alloy showed good cytocompatibility.
summary_en.validation: Corrosion rate measurements and in vitro cytocompatibility assays.
